purpose: Focused related-work context for the already frozen experiment; not a policy recommendation or a complete survey.
source_policy: Primary arXiv papers, official author project sites and author repositories only.

papers.title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
papers.claim: Samples several reasoning paths from one language model and aggregates final answers; reports improvements over greedy chain-of-thought on arithmetic and commonsense benchmarks.
papers.scope: Arithmetic and commonsense QA with models available in the original study; no DGX Spark or Nemotron serving measurement.
papers.prototype_match: Conceptual independent-sampling control for the full-plan ensembles and independent trajectories.
papers.important_difference: Our arithmetic ensembles accept any exactly verified solution, rather than selecting the modal answer. Code candidates are selected using feedback tests, then one frozen candidate receives holdout grading.

papers.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
papers.claim: One model generates an answer, critiques it, and revises it iteratively, without further training. Reports gains across seven tasks using contemporary GPT-family models.
papers.scope: Mixed tasks and human/automatic evaluation; not exclusively exact arithmetic or executable code correctness.
papers.prototype_match: Closest conceptual reference for sequential full-plan refinement and iterative code repair.
papers.important_difference: Our refinement receives objective verifier or executable feedback; the original method emphasizes model-generated self-feedback. Its reported gains do not quantify our feedback protocol.

papers.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
papers.claim: Maintains alternative intermediate thoughts and uses search with model evaluation, lookahead or backtracking. Demonstrates gains on Game of 24, creative writing and mini crosswords.
papers.scope: The original tasks, prompts, models and search budgets; not a measurement of independent GPU agents or shared attention KV.
papers.prototype_match: Closest established search framing for a coordinator retaining a common frontier and handing states to workers.
papers.important_difference: Our shared arithmetic frontier uses exact legal transitions, deduplication and deterministic hash selection; it does not use ToT heuristic evaluation. Countdown rules and datasets differ, so raw success percentages are not directly comparable.

papers.title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
papers.claim: Several instances of the same model propose answers, read peers and revise over debate rounds. The main setup uses three agents and two rounds; authors report gains over ordinary single-agent generation.
papers.scope: Reasoning/factuality tasks from the original paper; positive results are not a universal advantage over compute-matched independent sampling or sequential repair.
papers.prototype_match: Related to communicating/voting policies, especially code-review voting among candidate programs.
papers.important_difference: Our arithmetic democracy proposes and votes on legal moves, with exact terminal acceptance. It is not unrestricted natural-language debate, and its shared frontier is a different policy.

papers.title: Graph of Thoughts: Solving Elaborate Problems with Large Language Models
papers.kind: explicit logical graph with aggregation and feedback
papers.claim: Represents generated thoughts as graph nodes and dependencies as edges, permitting aggregation and feedback rather than only linear or tree-shaped reasoning.
papers.scope: Task-specific graph transformations and evaluation; examples include sorting and keyword counting. This is logical information organization, not distributed GPU-memory sharing.
papers.prototype_match: Relevant precedent for storing reusable intermediate states or verified code-test observations in coordinator memory.
papers.important_difference: Our dictionary/JSONL handoff is a small fixed protocol. It is not a reproduction of GoT transformations or evidence that shared memory alone improves quality.

papers.title: More Agents Is All You Need
papers.kind: same-model scaling through sampling and voting
papers.claim: Agent Forest studies scaling the number of sampled outputs and aggregating them by answer frequency or similarity. Reports gains across reasoning and generation tasks; gains rise then fall as inherent difficulty increases.
papers.scope: Several models and datasets; open-ended code aggregation uses similarity scoring, not our executable verifier. Reported accuracy scaling does not establish saturated-fleet efficiency.
papers.prototype_match: Direct prior art for the original many-small-agents idea and independent-size controls; step-wise voting is also related to move-level democracy.
papers.important_difference: Increasing sample count is not itself cooperation. Our any-verified-solution arithmetic selection and one-frozen-holdout code grading differ from majority/similarity voting.

papers.title: Stop Overvaluing Multi-Agent Debate -- We Must Rethink Evaluation and Embrace Model Heterogeneity
papers.earlier_title: If Multi-Agent Debate is the Answer, What is the Question?
papers.claim: Evaluates five debate methods on nine benchmarks with four base models. Debate often fails to beat chain-of-thought or self-consistency despite more inference computation; the authors also study heterogeneous models.
papers.scope: A critical position/evaluation paper, not a theorem that all debate fails or heterogeneous panels universally succeed.
papers.prototype_match: Context for preserving strong solo, independent-sampling and sequential controls alongside communicating policies.
papers.important_difference: Our experiment deliberately fixes one model and uses verifiable synthetic tasks. It cannot establish conclusions about heterogeneous teams or all agent applications.
evidence_reviewed: current arXiv abstract, title and version history

papers.title: The Cost of Consensus: Isolated Self-Correction Prevails Over Unguided Homogeneous Multi-Agent Debate
papers.venue: ArXiv metadata lists ACM Conference on AI and Agentic Systems; proceedings not separately verified
papers.claim: Main study: ten same-model agents, three rounds, three 7–8B models, GSM-Hard and a hard MMLU subset. Debate costs 2.1–3.4× more tokens than isolated revision with similar/lower accuracy.
papers.scope: The isolated-revision control retains ten tracks; it is not simply one agent. Appendix J shows output-format caps inflate one large negative gap; some Llama gaps are nonsignificant.
papers.prototype_match: Relevant to independent repair versus peer exposure, communication cost and consensus discarding correct candidates.
papers.important_difference: Unguided rationale exchange differs from our verified-state search and objective feedback. It does not establish our policies’ outcomes.
evidence_reviewed: full-text Section 3.3, Results and Appendix J

synthesis.claim: The core ideas already exist: same-model sampling/voting, debate, iterative revision and explicit intermediate-state search have established literature. Local serving and controlled policy accounting are the relevant scope here, not a claim to invent swarms.
Published findings are mixed. A gain over one greedy call does not isolate communication from additional samples, revision opportunities or token expenditure.
synthesis.status: Interpretation of reported comparisons, not a result from the local experiment

synthesis.claim: Independent RNG draws are not independent sources of knowledge: one model may repeatedly prefer the same wrong answer. Sharing peer answers additionally creates dependence. Conformity or consensus can therefore coexist with shared error; this review does not assert a measured local error correlation.
synthesis.status: Statistical/conceptual caution; no correlation coefficient or local effect estimated

synthesis.claim: Keep the inference distinct from the evidence: arithmetic any-exactly-verified success is not majority voting; code feedback passing is not proof of held-out correctness; shared-frontier search combines state handoff, deduplication and selection.
basis: prototype design supplied in prior task context
synthesis.status: Description of frozen design, not outcome-dependent analysis

synthesis.claim: None of these papers qualifies this four-Spark serving recipe or establishes its long-run reliability, GPU cost, useful solutions/minute, or a universal optimal agent count.

article_framing: We are testing which already-known ways of spending inference compute yield useful verified work on a fixed local fleet, with strong controls and explicit communication/queue costs. Results remain specific to the frozen model, tasks, budgets, verification and runtime.
boundaries: No partial local evaluation scores or raw traces opened.
No new policies proposed or tuned during the active run.
Dates are first arXiv submission dates; publication venue years and revised titles are separately labeled.
Numerical claims are scoped author reports, not reproduced measurements.
